post.title: Why NYC renters paid 15% of a year's rent to a broker
post.ig:
Before June 11, 2025, New York City renters often paid a broker fee of one month's rent up to 15% of a year's rent, even when the landlord hired the broker.
StreetEasy: upfront costs on NYC fee listings averaged $12,951 in 2024 (year to date, reported Dec 2024).
NYC's FARE Act (in effect June 11, 2025) and a Massachusetts state law (Aug 1, 2025): whoever hires the broker pays.
StreetEasy (May 2026): rents on broker-represented units about $46 a month higher (~1.1%), versus an average $5,862 broker fee avoided upfront. Our math: 12% of a year's rent at $3,500 a month is $5,040.
NYC DCWP logged 2,000+ FARE Act complaints and inquiries in the law's first year (The Real Deal, June 2026).
Sources: NYC DCWP, StreetEasy, Mass.gov, Boston.gov, The Real Deal.
